newsitem.title: NORWAY: Fokus Q1 after-tax profits up 56.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Fokus Q1 after-tax profits up 56.5 pct.

text.p: Fokus Bank, a takeover target in Norway's crowded financial sector, said on Tuesday higher interest income helped increase first-quarter after-tax profits by 56.5 percent to 182.5 million crowns ($26.2 million) from the same year-ago period.
It said the result corresponded to earnings per share of 11.1 crowns on an annual basis.
The bank, Norway's fourth largest, attributed the improved result to higher interest income, higher commissions and higher profits on securities.

"We are very satisfied with the result and see it as another confirmation that Fokus Bank has developed into a competitive and solid player in the Norwegian bank market," Managing Director Bjarne Borgersen said in a statement.
Fokus moved forward the date for its first-quarter result announcement by 10 days following a hostile takeover bid on Monday by Sparebankgruppen, which consists of sixteen regional savings banks.

Sparebanksgruppen was bidding 73 crowns per share for Fokus, which it valued at 4.80 billion. The group said it controlled, directly or indirectly, 10 percent of Fokus, which is 80 percent owned by foreign investors. ($ = 6.978 Norwegian Crowns)
